# Implications of the Fed’s Structural Shift

Report 178 | Published 2025-12-21 | Evaluated 2026-11-07

[Original member article](https://www.lynalden.com/premium-2025-12-21/) | [Article index](README.md) | [Structured review](../data/reviews/178.json)

Reserve normalization, emerging-market opportunities and metal caution.

Funding conditions improved as expected, and the yuan direction was right. Bitcoin and India floor calls failed. The Terra recap correctly highlights a prescient risk warning but omits an earlier relative-bullish stance. The December metal caution was timely, while the bank Treasury-holdings explanation conflates agencies with sovereign debt.

**Coverage:** Full numbered text and image inventory read. All material theses across macro, digital assets, investment analysis and concluding sections considered. Position listings and incidental descriptive statistics are excluded unless they support a thesis.

## Claims

### 178-C01

**Funding pressure should ease.**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Right |
| Type | forecast |
| Horizon | Coming weeks and months |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | 2026-funding-normalization |
| Source blocks | 8, 10 |
| Thesis family | 2026-funding-normalization |

The SOFR-IORB spread averaged +7.64 basis points before the December shift, +0.77 in Q1 2026 and -2.17 in April-October. Treasury-collateral overnight repo usage also declined on average; that series excludes agency collateral and is not total facility usage. Calendar spikes persisted, so “settle down” fits better than a claim of permanently zero facility use.

**Direction:** See assessment; evidence is limited to the stated proposition.

**Timing:** Coming weeks and months

**Mechanism:** Price direction alone does not identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Outcome evidence:**

- [SOFR observations through the audit cutoff](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/SOFR) | FRED / originating statistical agency | Verified in the audit

Daily common-date spread to IORB: November 1-December 9 +7.64bp; Q1 +0.77bp; April-October -2.17bp.

- [IORB observations through the audit cutoff](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/IORB) | FRED / originating statistical agency | Verified in the audit

Matched policy remuneration rate.

- [RPONTSYD observations through the audit cutoff](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/RPONTSYD) | FRED / originating statistical agency | Verified in the audit

Treasury-collateral overnight repo usage averaged $1.89bn in November 1-December 21 and $0.68bn in Q1. This is not total repo usage across eligible collateral.

Purchases began December 12, 2025 to maintain ample reserves; initial monthly amount about $40 billion. Technical reserve supply does not itself establish a change in the interest-rate stance.

The Desk purchased about $40 billion monthly ahead of expected April tax flows. The objective was maintaining ample reserves.

### 178-C03

**The balance sheet reaches roughly $7 trillion.**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Too early |
| Type | forecast |
| Horizon | End of 2026 |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |

The December 2026 endpoint remains in the future. Fed assets rose from $6.557 trillion on December 17, 2025 to $6.748 trillion on November 4, 2026. The arithmetic is a scenario, not a guaranteed minimum: purchases respond to reserve demand and other liabilities, not a binding 20%-of-GDP rule.

**Direction:** See assessment; evidence is limited to the stated proposition.

**Timing:** End of 2026

**Mechanism:** Price direction alone does not identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Next test:** Compare final December balance sheet with the approximate $7tn forecast and the purchase/reinvestment assumptions.

### 178-C18

**Dollar weakness eases emerging-market debt burdens.**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Right |
| Type | explanation |
| Horizon | Not specified |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | dollar-debt-currency-mismatch |
| Source blocks | 141, 142, 143 |
| Thesis family | dollar-debt-currency-mismatch |

For an unhedged borrower earning local currency and owing fixed dollars, dollar depreciation lowers the local-currency debt burden. Export revenues, hedges and local borrowing can offset or reverse exposure. A weaker exchange rate is not itself proof of abundant funding everywhere.

**Direction:** See assessment; evidence is limited to the stated proposition.

**Timing:** No fixed deadline stated.

**Mechanism:** Price direction alone does not identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Deductive assessment:**

- Fixed dollar obligation
- Local-currency income
- No offsetting dollar assets or hedge

Local-currency obligation equals dollars owed times local currency per dollar; a lower conversion rate reduces the burden.

## Framework lessons

- Preserve the complete original thesis when evaluating retrospective success stories.
- Separate a failed near-term floor from a still-open multi-year investment case.

## Verification limitations

- Current page snapshot is not an authenticated publication-date version.
- A missing horizon is not replaced with an invented author deadline.
- Market sensitivities use vendor adjusted closes and do not reconstruct portfolio execution.
